name: Polished Brown
lede: Polished Brown is ColorHub's direct English rendering of Tonocha, a reddish brown that Japanese tradition names for a kind of polished, whetstone-smoothed tea-brown surface.

sections.title: A whetstone-smooth brown
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Tonocha (礪茶), combining tono, a word tied to grinding or whetstones, with cha, "tea-brown," naming a smooth, burnished reddish brown [1]. ColorHub's English name, Polished Brown, translates the sense directly rather than loosely [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places the swatch in block 38, "dark reddish orange," about 6.3 units from that block's centre [2]. The library's nearest other named colors are [[dusty-sienna]] and [[sienna]], each under 3 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 43, chroma 38, hue 49 degrees, a moderately bright, warm reddish brown [2]. The library also records a second, greener alternate value for this name (#5A6457), a reminder that more than one reference swatch has carried the same Japanese name over time [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 1,092 of 23,781 paintings, about 5 percent, as photographed [3]. It plays a mid-tone role most often, 64 percent of its occurrences [3]. The Master of Alkmaar and Filippo Lippi each carry it at ten times or more the archive's overall rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the color word [[sienna]] at nearly ten times the ordinary rate, and its presence peaks in the 1440s, in 16 of 58 paintings [3].

openers: Polished Brown's Japanese name describes a whetstone-smoothed surface, and the library keeps two different reference swatches for it.
